🔊 Iran rejects speculation it plans to attack neighbors’ airports over US flight bans

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) has denied claims that the country would respond militarily to recent aviation restrictions, saying negotiations with the relevant countries to lift the unlawful restrictions are being seriously pursued and followed up.

The SNSC Secretariat issued a statement on Saturday in response to misleading reports on air transport, noting that the publication of inaccurate interpretations and false quotations attributed to the top security official regarding air transportation has raised questions and ambiguities.
​
The Council declared that claims suggesting Iran would resort to military retaliation in response to recent air restrictions are denied, emphasizing that the authorities are vigorously pursuing the air restriction issue.
​
The statement made clear that Iran has several non-military options available for reciprocal measures, which may be applied to certain airports if necessary, but expressed hope the situation does not reach that point.
​
The clarification came after some regional airports suspended flights, following US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s rhetoric about placing restrictions on Iranian airlines, including bans on flight operations and access to ground services.

📡 Sunni cleric stresses role of defensive power, diplomacy in regional security

📌 Bandar Abbas, IRNA – A prominent Sunni cleric in Hormozgan Province in southern Iran, Sheikh Hossein Bazmandegan, has stressed that lasting regional security depends on a combination of defensive capabilities, national cohesion, political prudence, and active diplomacy.

In an interview with IRNA on Saturday, Bazmandegan said that defensive capabilities are essential to protecting territorial integrity, national sovereignty, and the security of the people, and that this does not conflict with efforts toward dialogue and peace.
​
Referring to the Iranian president’s recent remarks at the UN General Assembly on the right to defend the country, he said that the Islamic Republic of Iran, while emphasizing its readiness to defend itself, has also stressed dialogue and the pursuit of peace.
​
He added that effective defensive capabilities create deterrence by increasing the costs and consequences of any military action for the aggressor, thereby helping prevent miscalculations.
​
Bazmandegan stressed that deterrence does not depend solely on weapons, but also requires defensive capabilities, national cohesion, political resolve, a resilient economy and active diplomacy.
​
He said defensive power and diplomacy are not rivals but should complement each other, as defensive power without diplomacy could lead to misperceptions and heightened tensions.
​
Referring to the importance of security in the Persian Gulf for the people of Hormozgan, he said security should be understood as more than military power, stressing the need to reduce tensions, build trust, and expand cooperation among regional countries.
​
Bazmandegan said that regional countries should establish regional security arrangements based on common interests and direct dialogue, while maintaining both the ability to defend their sovereignty and channels for negotiations to prevent war.
